title: Fraction
summary: A fraction is a part of a whole — like 3/4 of a pizza. The bottom number (denominator) tells how many equal parts the whole is split into; the top number (numerator) tells how many you have. Explore fractions as equal parts of a whole and of a group.

Finding a fraction of a group
plainLanguageExplanation: A fraction describes part of a whole. When you split a pizza into 4 equal slices and eat 3, you have eaten 3/4 (three quarters) of the pizza. The number on the bottom, the denominator, counts the equal parts the whole was split into — the 4 slices. The number on top, the numerator, counts how many of those parts you are talking about — the 3 eaten. The line between them is read as 'out of'. Fractions can also describe part of a group: 3/4 of 8 balls means 6 balls. If the numerator is smaller than the denominator, the fraction is less than 1, like 3/4; equal parts is what makes a fraction honest — every piece must be the same size.

keyFacts.label: Whole

whyItMatters: Fractions are how we share things fairly and measure partial amounts — half a cup, three quarters of an hour, a third of a budget. Fractions underpin decimals, percents, ratios, probability, and almost all of higher math.
didYouKnow: The word 'fraction' comes from the Latin 'fractus', meaning broken — a fraction is literally a broken-off piece of a whole.
compareReason: Two different-looking fractions can name the same amount — comparing 1/2 with 2/4 shows what equal parts really mean.
